# Purpose

This document imports stock data for the symbols listed in `portfolio.txt`,
computes basic statistics (moving average, mean, mode, median and standard
deviation), and displays the data and visualizations. Functions are defined
in `technical_analysis_functions.R`.

# 1. Install packages (run once)

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("quantmod", "TTR", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
```

# 2. Load functions and portfolio

```{r load-functions}
source("technical_analysis_functions.R")

symbols <- read_symbols("portfolio.txt")
symbols
```

# 3. Import stock data

Data is downloaded from Yahoo Finance with `quantmod` for 2025 and stored as
one data frame per symbol.

```{r import}
stocks <- load_stock_data("portfolio.txt",
                          from = "2025-01-01", to = "2025-12-31")
names(stocks)
```

# 4. Display imported data

```{r display-data}
display_stock_data(stocks, n = 5)
```

# 5. Basic statistics

```{r statistics}
stats <- calculate_all_statistics(stocks, ma_window = 20)
knitr::kable(stats$summary, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Basic statistics of closing prices (2025)")
```

# 6. Visualizations

## Closing price with 20-day moving average

```{r price-plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_price_with_ma(stocks[[sym]], sym, ma_window = 20)
}
```

## Trading volume

```{r volume-plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_volume(stocks[[sym]], sym)
}
```

## Statistics comparison

```{r stats-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_statistics_summary(stats$summary)
```
